parsed.attack: The author answers USCIS but names the wrong incumbent: it is Duolingo, which already runs a US citizenship course, already shipped unscripted spoken roleplay in Duolingo Max's Video Call, already bills by subscription, and already holds the daily attention of exactly this audience of adult ESL learners. 'Roleplay: your naturalization interview' is content configuration on live infrastructure, not a build, and Duolingo also owns the classroom and community distribution the loop depends on. A consumable-credits product carrying 20 to 80 dollars of acquisition cost per payer cannot survive the same rehearsal appearing as a bundled tier in the app the buyer already opens every morning.
parsed.strongest_defence: The personalized core requires ingesting the applicant's own filed N-400 so the officer can read back their travel dates and addresses and doubt them, and a listed consumer-education company will not take custody of immigration filings or simulate an adverse outcome, on unauthorized-practice and liability grounds, exactly as the author argues USCIS cannot. A gamified, encouraging product also cannot credibly ship adversarial pressure without breaking its own brand promise.
parsed.verdict_reason: Duolingo cannot ship the document-grounded, adversarial version, but it can ship a good-enough spoken mock into the same audience for free and take the paid demand with it.
